sections.name: Hook
lines: n_hook
Noise-cancelling headphones don't just block noise. They fight it, with more sound.
n_title
Here's how silence is made, in five steps.

sections.name: Sound is a wave
lines: n_wave
Step one. Sound is a wave of air pressure. Squeezed air, then stretched air, rolling towards your ear.
n_ear
Those waves push your eardrum in and out, and your brain hears that as sound.
n_pitch
Fast wiggles sound high-pitched. Slow ones sound low, like a rumble.

sections.name: Listening in
lines: n_mics
Step two. Tiny microphones on the outside of each ear cup listen to the noise around you.
n_inside
Another microphone inside the cup checks what actually reaches your ear.
n_passive
And even before any electronics, the padded cushions seal around your ears and soak up a lot of sound.

sections.name: The opposite wave
lines: n_flip
Step three. A chip creates the exact opposite wave. Where the noise pushes, it pulls. Where the noise pulls, it pushes.
n_cancel
Played through the speaker, the two waves meet and cancel out. Peaks fill the troughs, and the air barely moves.
n_fast
It has to keep adjusting thousands of times every second, because noise is always changing.

sections.name: What it beats best
lines: n_low
Step four. It works best on steady, low sounds, like engines, fans and the hum of a plane.
n_high
Sudden, high-pitched sounds, like voices or clattering plates, change too fast to cancel. The soft cushions block much of those instead.

sections.name: Tricks and quirks
lines: n_trans
Step five. Transparency mode flips the idea around. The outside microphones pass sound through, so you can hear the world.
n_pressure
And if you ever feel a strange pressure in your ears, nothing's actually pushing on them. Your brain just isn't used to the missing hum.
n_battery
It's also why noise cancelling uses battery. The chip and speaker keep working, even while you hear nothing.

sections.name: Recap
lines: w_recap
Sound is a wave. Microphones listen. A chip makes the opposite wave, and the two cancel out. Silence, made from sound.
outro
Next time you put them on, you'll know you're hearing anti-noise. Follow for more of the tech you use every day.
